newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Netcomm confirms merger with Banksia.
newsitem.headline: Netcomm confirms merger with Banksia.

text.p: Modem manufacturer Netcomm Ltd said on Thursday that it had signed an agreement to merge with its unlisted rival Banksia Technologies Pty Ltd.

The company, which said on July 14 that it planned to combine its analogue modem business with Banskia, said the merger would create Australia's largest supplier of personal computer communication products with annual sales of more than A$70 million.
Under the merger agreement, NetComm will acquire the assets and assume the liabilities of Banksia and also acquire Dataplex and Simple Computing, both owned by Banksia, NetComm said.

Shareholders of Banksia -- David Stewart, who owns 92.04 percent and Microcom Inc with 7.96 percent -- will be issued pro rata with 19.87 million shares in NetComm, representing 52 percent of its expanded share capital.
Microcom is a unit of Compaq Computer Corp.
It said Stewart will become the new managing director and principal shareholder of the merged group. The chairman will be George Maltby.
NetComm said it was in talks with potential buyers of its stake in the internet service provider Connect.com.au Pty Ltd.
"NetComm's current 33 percent shareholding in Connect is expected to be reduced in the near future when a further shareholding funding call is made," NetComm said.
"The (Banksia) merger is expected to generate very significant savings in the order of A$3 million per annum," it said. The two groups shipped over 250,000 products in 1996/97.
"The continuing growth in modem sales should result in the number of units shipped in 1997/98 exceeding 400,000 from the merged group," NetComm said.
For the year ending June 1997, both NetComm and Banksia achieved sales over A$30 million. The combined market share is likely to exceed 45 percent, NetComm said.

"The significant synergies expected from the merger will result in the merged group delivering enhanced profitability," NetComm said. It said other opportunities would be pursued by the merged group over the next 12 months.

It said the merger has to be approved by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), NetComm shareholders and its banker the Commonwealth Bank of Australia and National Australia Bank Ltd, Banksia's banker.
NetComm shares last traded at 60 cents on July 14.
